QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_4

question.text: Kaveri Private Equity Fund called INR 500 cr, distributes INR 1,200 cr at exit. Waterfall: ROC -> 8% pref (1 year, simple) -> 50/50 partial catch-up until GP reaches 20% of all profit above ROC -> 80/20 thereafter. Compute the GP's total CARRY.

explanation.text: The Logic: Return of capital: LP gets 500; pool left = 700. Preferred return: 8% * 500 = 40 to LP; pool left = 660. 50/50 catch-up runs until GP's cumulative carry equals 20% of total profit (profit = 700, target GP carry = 140). Let C be the catch-up amount (GP receives C/2 in this tier). After catch-up, the residual (660 - C) is split 80/20. Setting GP total = 140: 0.5C + 0.20*(660 - C) = 140, giving C = 26.67. GP carry = 13.33 + 0.20*633.33 = 140. Total GP carry = INR 140 cr, which equals 20% of the INR 700 cr profit. The Trap: INR 120 cr ignores the catch-up entirely. INR 132 cr applies 20% to profit-after-pref without the catch-up step. INR 108 cr mis-shares the preferred return. Note: A useful cross-check on partial catch-up math is that total GP carry should equal the agreed carry percentage applied to total profit above return of capital once the catch-up is fully completed.
